# What's inside

The libraries AF is built on, what each one does here and what AF adds on top. **Core** is the free foundation every game gets; **Plus** is the paid Automata Plus tier (PRODUCT spec §1, PD-1).

Versions are the exact pins in [versions.md](versions.md) (the vendored Ruken tarballs show their packed version and RukenApp commit). Licenses are read from each installed package's `package.json`. A library AF has chosen but not installed yet says so and names the task that installs it.

## PixiJS 8

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `pixi.js` | 8.21.0 | MIT |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Draws the game in 2D: WebGL2 by default, WebGPU opt-in per game (ADR 0002).
- **Why it was chosen:** Both reference games render with Pixi 8: FloorFifty in 2D and The Last Light in 3D. Ruken's manifest declares `webgl2` and no WebGPU value, so the WebGL2 path is the one that must stay solid (ADR 0002).
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-render-pixi`: the `./no-eval` entry every game imports first (Ruken's CSP has no `eval`), renderer start-up with a WebGL2 default, a `RenderDelta` consumer that interpolates between sim ticks, the letterbox and canvas resolution, and GLSL + WGSL filter-program pairs.

## Koota

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `koota` | 0.6.6 | ISC |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** The entity-component store inside the deterministic sim (ADR 0001).
- **Why it was chosen:** Spike S1 found it deterministic across Node, Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, like Miniplex, and it adds relations with data, added/changed/removed tracking and struct-of-arrays storage at no determinism cost (ADR 0001).
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-sim` keeps Koota behind a facade: its own monotonic `StableId` (Koota recycles IDs), StableId-ordered iteration, snapshot and restore, render deltas, seeded RNG, deterministic math and hashing, and `.replay` recording. Game code never imports Koota directly.

## Effect

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `effect` | 3.22.2 | MIT |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Runs everything outside the sim: runtime services, the boot program, time, retries and resource disposal (ADR 0003).
- **Why it was chosen:** The runtime needs ordered boot with failure states, retries and timeouts, disposal on screen exit and restart, an injectable clock and typed errors that each map to a UI state; FloorFifty and The Last Light do all of that by hand (ADR 0003).
- **What AF adds on top:** Runtime managers are Effect services (`Context.Tag` + `Layer`), time comes from `Clock` and is tested with `TestClock`, and `Scope` replaces FloorFifty's `DisposeBag`. The sim never imports Effect (`check-boundaries` rejects it there) and the frame loop allocates no Effect per frame.

## Zod

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `zod` | 4.6.6 | MIT |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Every schema: content files, sim command and event payloads, and saved settings.
- **Why it was chosen:** Ruken's protocol and manifest are written in Zod at the same version, so AF and Ruken share one schema language; Effect Schema is not adopted (ADR 0003).
- **What AF adds on top:** Zod runs jitless under the `render-pixi/no-eval` entry so it works under Ruken's CSP; the content compiler turns Zod issues into `file:line:col` diagnostics.

## Svelte 5

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `svelte` | 5.57.1 | MIT |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Menus, HUD and every screen outside the canvas, with rune stores for app state (master spec §3).
- **Why it was chosen:** FloorFifty's UI and Ruken's own `packages/ui` are Svelte, and Ruken requires a mobile layout under `display.metrics` on phones (master spec §4.1).
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-ui`: mobile-first primitives (ScreenFrame, ActionBar, CornerControls, ScrollList, Dialog, LoaderOverlay, ErrorPanel), the single geometry owner (form factor, height tier, viewport tracking), focus navigation and browser hygiene, with layout-contract test helpers.

## Paraglide

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `@inlang/paraglide-js` | 2.25.4 | MIT |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Compiles the content compiler's locale keys into typed `t()` message functions (PRODUCT spec §4).
- **Why it was chosen:** FloorFifty already ships its localization on Paraglide, and Ruken asks every game to localize from `session.locale` (PRODUCT spec §4).
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-runtime` (PRODUCT.L1): language negotiation (the player's saved choice, then Ruken's `session.locale`, the browser, the default) before the first screen, a typed `t()` over Paraglide's runtime, `Intl` formatting and `<html lang dir>`. Planned in PRODUCT.L2 to L4: per-locale content, glyph coverage, the `xx-long` pseudo-locale in every layout contract and a language picker.

## smol-toml

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `smol-toml` | 1.9.0 | BSD-3-Clause |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Parses the TOML files under a game's `content/` (M1.3 content spec §8).
- **Why it was chosen:** FloorFifty's content compiler and Ruken both use it at this version.
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-content` validates the parsed TOML with Zod, reports `file:line:col` diagnostics, writes canonical JSON with a content hash, generates TypeScript types, the locale keys and Ruken manifest fields, and runs as a Vite plugin with watch mode.

## Ruken SDK

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `@ruken/sdk` | 0.0.0 (vendored tarball, RukenApp `b30d31b`) | not declared in the installed package |
| `@ruken/sdk-host` | 0.0.0 (vendored tarball, RukenApp `b30d31b`) | not declared in the installed package |
| `@ruken/manifest` | 0.0.0 (vendored tarball, RukenApp `b30d31b`) | not declared in the installed package |
| `@ruken/cli` | 0.0.0 (vendored tarball, RukenApp `b30d31b`) | not declared in the installed package |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** The host: the game side of Ruken's protocol, a fake host for tests, the manifest checks and CSP headers, and `ruken publish` (ADR 0004).
- **Why it was chosen:** Ruken is the reference host. FloorFifty already runs through these packages, so AF consumes them instead of re-deriving Ruken's contract (ADR 0004). They are vendored as tarballs until Ruken publishes them (`vendor/ruken/README.md`).
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-host`: the `Hosting` Effect service with typed errors and a test layer on the fake host; `@mcthaydt/automata-ship` generates `ruken.toml`, checks it with `@ruken/manifest` and hands the build to `ruken publish`.

## Vite, Vitest, Playwright

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `vite` | 8.3.3 | MIT |
| `vitest` | 5.0.3 | MIT |
| `@playwright/test` | 1.63.0 | Apache-2.0 |

- **Tier:** Core
- **What it does in AF:** Vite builds every game and example; Vitest runs unit tests and the cross-engine parity suites; Playwright drives browser journeys and the parity browsers.
- **Why it was chosen:** Ruken pins the same tools and versions, so a game and its host build and test the same way (versions.md).
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-testing`: sim and replay goldens that must match bit for bit in Node, Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, renderer-free screen fixtures and layout assertions (hit testing, target size, clipping); `automata-content`'s Vite plugin compiles content on build.

## Rapier (deterministic-compat)

Installed in mcthaydt/automata-plus, not in this repository; its versions are pinned there. Packages: `@dimforge/rapier2d-deterministic-compat`, `@dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic-compat`.

- **Tier:** Plus
- **What it does in AF:** 2D and 3D physics inside the sim (M2.1).
- **Why it was chosen:** The deterministic build gives bit-identical results in Node, Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, and `-compat` inlines the wasm, so there is no loader to set up (versions.md). The Last Light already uses Rapier 0.21.
- **What AF adds on top:** `@mcthaydt/automata-physics`: a sim plugin that syncs bodies in, steps and syncs out each tick, adds its own snapshot section and raises collision events, with four-engine parity tests. It lives in `automata-plus` (PRODUCT.5f) and left this repository in PRODUCT.5g.

## Colyseus

Not yet installed; planned for M7 (`net` and `server`). Package: `colyseus`.

- **Tier:** Plus
- **What it does in AF:** Rooms and transport for the `net` and `server` extensions (master spec §4).
- **Why it was chosen:** FloorFifty's multiplayer already runs on Colyseus: its network manager, room store and server rooms are the extraction source (extraction map).
- **What AF adds on top:** Planned in M7: a `NetworkPort` behind the client, a room-mirroring store, server rooms running the same sim, an input queue and tick scheduler, prediction and reconciliation.

## Why FloorFifty's Planck becomes Rapier

FloorFifty simulates its races with Planck. AF uses Rapier instead: Rapier's deterministic build is already proven across Node, Chromium, WebKit and Firefox (M2.1), and one physics engine means one parity suite (PRODUCT spec §8, PD-2).
